Costa Rica is home to around 1.6 million cattle.

Brahman cows are a popular breed in Costa Rica due to their ability to thrive in the country's tropical climate. They are known for their distinctive large ears and humps on their backs.

Livestock farming has contributed significantly to deforestation in the past, but recent measures are improving the management of pastureland, soil and water, and the integration of trees into livestock farming systems.
